messages:
maya: heads-up — been noodling on per-tenant escrow buckets for canary rollouts. idea: allocate a small token budget for each tenant for the rollout window so a noisy canary can be automatically contained instead of blowing tenant quotas or overall cost. thoughts?

sam: interesting. how would this play with existing rate quotas and Dedicated capacity? would escrow be separate or carved out of their quota?

maya: carveout seems cleaner — a temporary buffer on top of normal quota but enforced during rollout. if escrow is exhausted we auto-pause the rollout for that tenant (not the whole service).

dina: auto-pause per-tenant is good. we should define pause_thresholds: 80% used in first 10m => pause + notif. also add a cooldown window to avoid thrashing.

luis: what about fallback routing? when a tenant escrow hits 80% we should route new traffic to a lower-cost model variant or divert to stable version. UX should show "reverted to safe model" in console.

maya: agreed. proposed guard config snippet: 
```yaml
guard:
  mode: tenant_escrow
  escrow_alloc: ${per_tenant_tokens} # e.g. 10k tokens
  window: 1h
  pause_threshold: 0.8
  cooldown: 15m
  fallback_policy: route_to(stable_small)
  telemetry: [escrow_alloc, escrow_used, escrow_pauses]
```

sam: looks good. question: where do we enforce this? at the routing proxy or at runtime (model server)? enforcement at router lets us reroute quickly; at runtime gives more accurate token counting.

dina: we already have token-accurate counters in the runtime. router has coarse metrics. maybe do enforcement as a two-phase flow: router pre-check based on last-known counters, runtime authoritative and can veto. rollback-bot should also annotate the rollout if runtime veto happens.

rollout-bot: canary 231 started for tenant=acme, escrow_alloc=10000, window=1h

luis: console UX note — show per-tenant escrow burn rate and "time-to-threshold" ETA on the rollout page. add a small CTA to increase escrow or pause manually.

eng-console-bot: created dashboard tile "Escrow Burn (tenant)" in /rollouts/dashboards — shows top 10 tenants by burn rate.

sam: telemetry needs: escrow_alloc, escrow_used, escrow_pauses, pause_reason, fallback_model, pause_initiator. emit these as tags on traces and metrics so alerts and regressions can be tied to specific prompts.

maya: also think about economic guard: if estimated token cost during window exceeds X% of tenant monthly budget, escalate to manual review instead of auto-pause. some tenants expect burst and will accept higher cost.

dina: good call. add an "escrow_policy: opt_out|opt_in|auto|manual_escalate" flag in config. default auto.

maya: action items: i'll prototype enforcement flow + a small sim to show false positive rates. dina, can you mock console tiles and ETA? luis, help with fallback UX copy. sam, can you sketch router pre-check API?

sam: yep, will stub preflight API: `POST /v1/rollout/preflight` payload minimal {tenant, rollout_id, token_estimate}. returns {allow:true/false, reason}.

luis: will do UX mock. +1 on cooldown and ETA. :thumbsup:

dina: will wire dashboard and add alert rule: escrow_used > 0.85*escrow_alloc for 2 consecutive mins -> notify rollout owners + ops.

maya: nice. if the sim looks good i'll open a RFC next week. thanks everyone. :sparkles:
